doc.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Counting his blessings
summary: He reflects on his good life, fishing, gardening and family.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Bobby, when I look past you, I look out into your yard, and I think about our dinner last night, where you talked about all the things that bring joy into your life, going fishing, working in your garden, chopping wood, and spending time with Rosemary here by the fire, it seems like you’ve had a good life.
And you seem to enjoy it.

I count my blessings. I’m very lucky. I’ve very lucky to be able to sit here with you guys right here, with Rosemary, with our family and our children, to be able to sit here in this house. Think of all – to be able to have the health to be able to talk about the things that we’ve been talking about, to be able to remember the stories.
